messages:
Maria Garcia: quick Q from Finly's SOC2 form — do we ever forward raw request bodies to any third-party log processors (e.g. Datadog, Logflare) as part of our async pipeline? customer expects a short yes/no + explanation.
Ryan Chen: short answer: no for hosted. our service code strips bodies before emitting structured events. we only forward metadata + request_id/event_type/timing.
Sarah K.: curious about debug mode — any chance full payloads end up in a debug bucket or support logs? Finly will hammer us on exceptions.
Ryan Chen: good call — debug traces can contain payloads but those are written to an internal debug S3 bucket with strict ACLs and are encrypted with our KMS. access requires an approvals ticket (eng-infra) and is audited. retention is 7 days. not sent to external processors.
Jamal (infra): to add — our log-forwarder (internal svc) sends only structured logs to third-party processors. it's explicitly configured to drop body fields: we have a small transform that does body = "[REDACTED]" before forwarding.
sec-oncall-bot: snippet of transform rule (from logs-forwarder config):
```
filters:
  - if: has_field("body")
    then: set("body", "[REDACTED]")
```
Maria Garcia: perfect. what about Private/VPC customers who self-host — do we need special wording?
Ryan Chen: for Private deployments the customer controls the forwarders. we provide the same code with the redaction-by-default behavior, but if the customer configures a forwarder to include bodies, that's their responsibility. we can note: "default product behaviour redacts sensitive content; customers can change logging config in private deployments and should document subprocessors."
Sarah K.: subprocessors list for hosted: AWS (S3, Kinesis), Datadog (metrics/logs), Logflare for dev logs, and our build partner (HashCorp Vault for secrets). can we confirm exact product names for the questionnaire?
Jamal (infra): I can paste the approved subprocessor list into the ticket — also note that keys are Redwood-managed KMS for hosted. For customers requesting CMK we support it in Private via BYOK/HSM.
Maria Garcia: final ask — access controls statement. short bullet for SOC2: who can view raw debug buckets, how is access requested, and where it's logged?
Ryan Chen: suggest this copy: "Raw request bodies are not forwarded to external subprocessors. Limited debug traces that may include bodies are stored in an encrypted internal bucket; access is granted only to on-call or engineers via a documented approval process and is logged in our access audit trail. Hosted keys are Redwood-managed; Customer-managed keys are available for Private deployments."
Sarah K.: +1. add retention and encryption details: "retention 7 days; AES-256 encryption with KMS-wrapped keys; access requests tracked in Jira ticket and CloudTrail."
Maria Garcia: awesome, I'll send that back to Finly. linking runbook: https://go/internal/runbooks/log-redaction for reviewers. thanks all :pray:
Ryan Chen: lmk if you want me to include the config snippet or JAMAL to paste subproc list in the reply.
Jamal (infra): I'll drop the subproc list into the ticket and cc security.
Maria Garcia: done — closing this thread, will paste customer-facing text and ping here for signoff.
